"'''The Felix Klein Protocols'''" is a collection of handwritten records of the [[University of Göttingen|Göttingen]] seminar lectures of [[Felix Klein]] and his school. They span over 8000 pages in 29 volumes, and are regarded as one of the richest records of mathematical activity in modern times.<ref name="Notices">{{Cite journal
  | last1 = Chislenko
  | first1 = Eugene
  | last2 = Tschinkel
  | first2 = Yuri
  | title = The Felix Klein Protocols
  | journal = [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]
  | volume = 54
  | pages = 960–970
  | date = September 2007
  | issue = 8
  }}</ref>
The previously unpublished Klein Protocols were made available digitally in 2006.<ref>{{cite web|title=Felix Klein, Klein Protokolle|url=http://www.uni-math.gwdg.de/aufzeichnungen/klein-scans/|language=de|access-date=2011-08-04|archive-date=2022-09-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220924223422/https://www.uni-math.gwdg.de/aufzeichnungen/klein-scans/|url-status=live}}</ref> The collection has been compiled by Eugene Chislenko and [[Yuri Tschinkel]].

A searchable index of the protocols can be found at [http://page.mi.fu-berlin.de/moritz/klein/ ''Felix Klein Protokolle''].

==Years covered==
From 1872 to 1896 Klein conducted his seminars alone, mainly in [[pure mathematics]].  The years 1897–1913 show collaborations with mathematicians such as [[David Hilbert]], [[Karl Schwarzschild]], [[Ludwig Prandtl]], [[Carl Runge]] and [[Hermann Minkowski]].
